content: It appears to be a bibliography or citation list from a scientific or academic document.g., APA, MLA, or Chicago) or summarize the key information from each reference. 1. A study conducted by Kikafunda JK, Walker AF, Collett D, and Tumwine JK in 1998 explored the risk factors contributing to early childhood malnutrition in Uganda. The findings were published in the journal Pediatrics, volume 102, under the article identifier e45. 2. Kim HJ, Kwon H, Oh SW, Lee CM, Joh HK, Kim Y, Um YJ, and Ahn SH in 2015 investigated the association between breastfeeding and postmenopausal bone loss. Their research, based on data from the Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey, was published in the Korean Journal of Family Medicine, volume 36, issue 5, pages 216-220. 3. In 2020, Kim KM and Choi JW examined the relationship between breastfeeding and cognitive function in children from early childhood to school age. This prospective birth cohort study was published in the International Breastfeeding Journal, volume 15, article 83. 4. Kondolot M, Poyrazoglu S, Horoz D, Borlu A, Altunay C, and colleagues in 2017 identified risk factors for overweight and obesity in children aged 2 to 6 years. Their findings were published in the Journal of Pediatric Endocrinology and Metabolism. 5. Krenz-Niedbała M, Kościński K, Puch EA, Zelent A, and Bręborowicz A in 2015 explored whether the relationship between breastfeeding and childhood risks of asthma and obesity is mediated by infant antibiotic treatment. Their study was published in Breastfeeding Medicine, volume 10, issue 6, pages 326-333. 6. Kvale G and Heuch I in 1987 investigated the relationship between lactation and cancer risk, with a specific focus on breast cancer. Their findings were published in the Journal of Epidemiology and Community Health, volume 42, pages 30-37. 7. A Korean women's cohort study published in the International Journal of Cancer in 2003 examined the effect of lifetime lactation on breast cancer risk. The study was detailed in volume 105, pages 390-393. 8. Lee SY, Kim MT, Jee SH, and Yang HP in 2005 conducted a study to determine whether long-term lactation protects premenopausal women against hypertension risk. Their findings were published in Preventive Medicine, volume 41, pages 433-438. 9. Lee H, Park H, Ha E, Hong YC, Ha M, Park H, Kim BN, Lee B, Lee SJ, Lee KY, Kim JH, Jeong KS, and Kim Y in 2016 studied the effect of breastfeeding duration on cognitive development in infants. This three-year follow-up study was published in the Journal of Korean Medical Science, volume 31, issue 4, pages 579-584. 10. Li F, Lin J, Ying X, Qiu Y, Li S, Zhai Y, Zhang T, Wang X, Gu X, Wu M, and He F in 2020 reported a U-shaped association between breastfeeding duration and cognitive impairment in Chinese postmenopausal women. Their findings were published in Scientific Reports, volume 10, article 6584.
